notes: This Strategy should be combined with a fast paced mapping strategies to complete your "inbetween maps" as fast as possible. My personal recommendation is Deli Boss Rushing, as it sets up your atlas with Grand Mirrors, whilst also having a nice flow of consistent currency.
Chase "Anomaly Maps" on the infinite Atlas. Travel out into the fog, searching for red/blue beams, path towards them and complete the maps with the respective setup on the left.

Rakiata's Flow and Garukhan's Resolve are chase Lineage Gems from Jade Isle and Sacred Reservoir respectively. These are always worth a large chunk of divines, keeping this strategy relevant at all stages of the league.

These Lineage Gems are scaled through 1) Jados passive, Untold Histories and 2) The Atlas Tree Forest Mastery node, with the increased Lineage Gem drop rate selected - when combined with the Mastered Domain unique tablet with the Forest Biome rolled, you can turn every Jade Isle / Sacred Reservoir into a Forest Biome.
Visions of Paradise allows you to run the Sacred Reservoir / Jade Isle maps twice. This should always be used on Sacred Reservoir, and can be used on Jade Isle depending on prices / your preference.
Citadel Bosses drop valuable fragments. These fragments are scaled through waystone drop chance both through your Waystone/Tablets.
When running the map twice thanks to Visions of Paradise, you do not need to use another Mastered domain tablet as the node is now a forest biome.

farms.waystone: T15 Waystone, HAS TO BE 5 MODS - Then craft with an Omen of Chaotic Rarity, Quantity and Effectiveness simultaneously. Exalt afterwards.
farms.rarity: Rarity is Mandatory. Aim for 100-120% Rarity on your gear with this strategy.
notes: The Waystone craft on the right guarantees 103% monster rarity on your Waystones.

Run a Delirium Strategy to spawn Grand Mirrors. Run those Grand mirrors with a non juiced strategy as after the recent nerfs they no longer provide double tablet effect. Spread Delirium Fog onto City biomes (you cannot pick exactly where you spread the fog to, but pick the option closest to a City Biome).
Run these Delirium Fog City Biomes for an Extra Tablet Slot thanks to the Atlas Tree node Industrial Improvements.
You run 4 different tablets to scale Hildas Ancient Inscriptions node. The best second modifier for each tablet would be "inc number of rare monsters" this hikes the investment greatly though.
Pull abyss rares out of the black void when they spawn to get high tier omens, or wait for the void to temporarily despawn before killing them.

farms.name: Jackpot Ritual

mods: As low of an increased tribute roll as you can afford
Ritual altars allow rerolling favours 3 additional times

farms.rarity: Rarity is not mandatory as this is not a ground loot focused farm.
notes: This strategy is best ran on city biomes to add a fourth tablet slot. There are budget alternatives that opts out of using city biomes / ritual altars allow rerolling favours additional times to reduce the investment greatly.
This strategy is for jackpot hunting and is feast or famine. A more consistent ritual hunting strategy with less heights would be the other one listed in S tier.

Use the Head of the King. This item is used at Caer Tarth, the ritual area on the atlas. Select a city map if possible. This item allows you to make a chain of 6 juiced ritual maps, which will then be modified to buff your ritual encounters.

On your Head of the King modified maps, look for the best modifiers and complete that map first, so it spreads to future maps in the chain. The best modifier you can get and spread is "ritual altars offer % increased number of favours."

Try and get a modifier that helps with your tribute gain/cost on your reroll tablets. These will likely come at a premium, but you may have some tribute issues without a sufficient amount of these modifiers.

farms.name: Tablet Farming
farms.waystone: T15 Waystone, 6 Mod Corrupted with 90% Waystone Drop Chance.
farms.tip: Focus on Mountain/City Biomes for either % inc tablets dropped or a fourth tablet slot.
notes: The chance to drop a league mechanic specific tablet drops significantly if you are using that tablet (for example, if you are running an abyss tablet your odds of dropping one is lowered).
Irradiated tablets add a random league mechanic to your Map - These league mechanics wont have the diminishing returns on tablet drops, creating a random tablet farm for every mechanic in the game.

Run your maps normally, completing all of the random league mechanics that spawn in it. For Ritual you do not need to run the altar, just kill the naturally spawned mobs on it. For temple, complete the circle and open the chest.

Uncrafted or crafted, tablets are expensive and will always be relevant. If you are interested in crafting your tablets for profit, look through this entire spreadsheet to see which tablets strategies run, and sell those when you roll them.

farms.name: Aldur's Saga / Rumour Hunting
farms.tip: With logbooks having their drop rates directly buffed through the new expedition tree, and with Aldur's Saga becoming more popular, this strategy is cheaper than ever before and more profitable than ever before.
notes: In the ocean biome at the bottom right of the atlas, the unique map "Moor of the fallen skies" may spawn. Chain all of the X's to the final Verisium encounter, then select Aldur's Saga as your reward.
The rumour "Fallen Stars" means that Moor of the Fallen Skies spawns. Keep an eye out for this rumour, and as soon as you see it use a logbook and collect your Aldur's Saga.
When using a logbook, path towards the outside of the area to unlock the ability to use more logbooks. Try and path through grand expeditions to increase your odds at getting good Verisium Runes.
Aldur's Saga modifies grand expeditions. Modifiers include: Every Verisium Remnant has at least (5/6/7) slots. You can either use it yourself, or sell it for a lot of money.
I recommend selling your Aldur's Sagas as they are priced around people hunting for permanent stats to min-max their characters. You likely will lose money using them yourself.

The loot explosions from Remnants are directly scaled by 1) How many rune slots a remnant has and 2) which rune slots it has. For example, a 7/8/9 slot Remnant may spawn with "increased monster rarity" "monsters transfer mods on death" "slain monsters may respawn as a higher rarity." These greatly increase the loot dropped.

farms.name: Grand Expedition Farming
farms.waystone: T15 Waystone rolled for Monster Effectiveness and Rarity of Items Found
farms.tip: Grand Expedition can be feast or famine, with long dry streaks being broken up by massive jackpots. Because of this, efficiency is key and its best to focus on more remnants seen than it is to juice the loot explosions from them.
notes: Doryani and Jado are both good choices for this. Doryani is better for scaling loot dropped by monsters, Jado is better for specifically farming the Verisium Remnant rewards.
For pure loot tile efficiency, check your Map for lucrative remnants (6+ slots typically, although some 5s can be worth a good bit) and only blow up the good remnants.

With the most recent expedition buffs including the new atlas tree, chaining verisium remnants from the lowest rune to the highest rune can result in juicy loot explosions. Highlighted runes are added to future remnants, so prioritise the good highlighted runes early on in your chain.
If you get a "dud" grand expedition, you can place one explosive and blow it up to complete the map and move on.
League mechanic specific tablets, and overseer tablets do not apply to Grand Expeditions. Irradiated does.

farms.name: Unstable Hiveblood farming
farms.tip: Always keep an eye on catalyst prices. If significant time has passed and the market has shifted, the tree setup may be outdated and farming for jewel catalysts may be better.
notes: This strategy is focused purely on farming hiveblood to craft either catalysts, rings or amulets with on your tree. All of the profit comes from spending the hiveblood.
I have not tested ring crafting yet.

For amulet farming, you are trying to drop Absent amulets which can roll a number of different spirit skills. A lot are around a divine, a couple are around 2-3 divines (cast on dodge/crit) and trinity is hovering around 10 divines.
Ilvl 82 ring/amulet wombgifts enable T1 Ele resist / attributes rolls. I do not think the extra premium is worth it in the case of crafting amulets, since you're focused on crafting the base.

Jados reworked partial transitions node is a nice buff to this strategy. It went from 20% chance to double the effect of your tablets, to a guaranteed 0-40% inc effect every map. This has greatly increased the consistency of farming hiveblood.
If you can, try and pair Monster effectiveness / rare monster effectiveness alongside your tablets. A much more expensive option would be the additional rare monsters when stabilised modifier.

farms.name: Hilda Logbook Farming
farms.waystone: 6 Modded T15 Corrupted with 90%+ Waystone Chance. Ran on regular Map nodes (not Grand Expedition)
farms.tip: Hilda is far and away the best master for farming logbooks. If logbook prices crash, then you could burn them yourself to hunt for Aldur's Saga. Its a loop that will always keep Expedition worth running.
notes: Logbooks drop from Verisium Remnants + Expedition Markers/Flags in normal maps. They are rare. It is theorized that waystone chance increases logbook drop rates.
Verisium Remnants apply an extra rune to future Remnants. For example, if you chain a 5 slot Verisium remnant to a 6 slot remnant, the final wave of that encounter will have 7 runes applied.

The loot explosions from Remnants are directly scaled by 1) How many rune slots a remnant has and 2) which rune slots it has. For example, a 7/8/9 slot Remnant may spawn with "increased monster rarity" "monsters transfer mods on death" "slain monsters may respawn as a higher rarity." These greatly increase the loot dropped.
Hilda is used to add more rare monsters to your expedition encounters, increasing the odds that you drop logbooks.
When running your expedition encounters, target high value remnants and as many monster markers / flags as you can fit in your expedition explosions.

m: 6 Modded T15 Corrupted with 90%+ Waystone Chance. Ran on regular Map nodes (not Grand Expedition)

farms.name: Big Boom Expedition
farms.waystone: 6 Modded T15 Corrupted with 90%+ Waystone Chance. Ran on regular Map nodes (not Grand Expedition)
farms.tip: This strategy is kind of completely outdone by Hilda logbook farming, and i wouldnt recommend doing it unless you literally want to turn off your brain and place one big bomba.
notes: Logbooks drop from Verisium Remnants + Expedition Markers/Flags in normal maps. They are rare. It is theorized that waystone chance increases logbook drop rates.
Verisium Remnants apply an extra rune to future Remnants. For example, if you chain a 5 slot Verisium remnant to a 6 slot remnant, the final wave of that encounter will have 7 runes applied.

With Big Boom expedition, every Verisium Remnant in the one explosion applies that rune to the other remnants. For example, if you have 3 Verisium Remnants with 5 rune slots, the final wave for all of those encounters has 7 runes.
Big Boom Expedition activates every Remnant at the same time, rather than one at a time. This saves a lot of time and is the main reason to run Big Boom Expedition in regular Maps.

The loot explosions from Remnants are directly scaled by 1) How many rune slots a remnant has and 2) which rune slots it has. For example, a 7/8/9 slot Remnant may spawn with "increased monster rarity" "monsters transfer mods on death" "slain monsters may respawn as a higher rarity." These greatly increase the loot dropped.
The Big Boom Master passive applies to Grand Expeditions, essentially bricking them as you only have one explosive. Do not run that Master passive with Grand Expeditions.

m: 6 Modded T15 Corrupted with 90%+ Waystone Chance. Ran on regular Map nodes (not Grand Expedition)
